_evidence: Command dispatcher 0x00540574: eax = ([0x7a97b0] >> 24) & 0x7f; 'cmp eax,0xc; ja' skips everything; 'cmp eax,9; je' skips the handler; else 'call [0x8307d8+4*cmd]' with esi = 0x7a97b4 (the packet after the command word), then 0xff stores to 0x81e4fb/0x81e4fe/0x82fd78, the header test (mhdr_00540574) and 0xff to 0x82fd5f, eax = -1, and always dword [0x7a97ac] = 0. Command word values: every command 0..12 (9 twice), with and without bit 31 and low-bit noise, plus 0x0d/0x7f (> 0xc). The 13-entry handler table 0x8307d8 is only read (its sole xref is this routine); its image entries are the game's handlers, most unverified and deep (0x5405dc runs 0x5030a0, 0x5407f7 a chain of [0xae6ca4] calls) and entry 12 is NULL in the image (the game never sends command 12). Per the lead's rule for indirect calls, every entry is drawn from mapped, already-verified register-only routines that read no stack argument and write no memory: 0x5405db/0x540883/0x5408d3 (the table's own 'ret' entries 0/6/9), 0x539f40 (loads 4 signed words of [esi] into ebx/eax/ebp/ecx and advances esi by 8 - like the real handlers 0x540825/0x5408d4/0x541949 it consumes packet bytes and moves esi), 0x5582f7 (esi += 4), 0x545f81 (inc esi) and 0x52bebb (dl = f(dl, al)). So the registers the handler leaves (ebx/ecx/edx/ebp/esi) differ from the entry values in many cases. Packet bytes 0x7a97b4..+0xf random (read by 0x539f40). Stored-to bytes 0x81e4fb/0x81e4fe/0x82fd78/0x82fd5f and the dword 0x7a97ac are varied so every store is visible.
